agent_notes: The text gives no number for Isaac's age, only 'old' and 'dim eyes'. I anchor on his birth with 123 years, which is Rashi's count at 27:2 (from Seder Olam: Isaac 123, Jacob 63). That gives c. 1943 BCE, which is later than Esau's marriage at 40 (c. 1967 BCE, Gen 26:34) and agrees with Jacob 63. The margin of 5 years covers the uncertainty of the count. The tier is MACRO_ERA because the age comes from the tradition and not from the text. Against the anchor chain, anchor.jacob_birth plus 63 years would give about the same date.

Targum Pseudo-Jonathan sets the scene on the night of 14 Nisan (Passover night) at 27:1 and 27:6. This is a midrashic dating that the Hebrew does not support, so I did not use it. The day, the season and the hour stay open.

אָנֹכִי עֵשָׂו בְּכֹרֶךָ is grammatically open: 'I [am] Esau, your firstborn' (the flat lie) or, as Rashi reads it, 'I [am the one bringing it]; Esau is your firstborn'. The five English versions all take the flat reading. I render the Hebrew without a copula in the literal layer so the ambiguity stays visible, and the dramatic layer follows the plain reading, since the narrative (v. 24 'Are you my son Esau?') treats it as a claim of identity.

הִקְרָה (from קרה, 'to meet, to cause to happen') is rendered 'made [it] meet before me'. agent_notes: Игра «сеирот» (косматые) и «Сеир» русским словом «косматые» не передаётся; она оставлена только в примечании. Имя Исав в Синодальном даёт также прилагательное «Исавовы» (ст. 22), в литеральном слое выбрано «Исава».
Нефеш в буквальном слое — «моя душа»: так читает и Синодальный перевод; в комментарии и заметке объяснено, что это не бесплотная часть человека, а всё его существо и жажда жизни.
Имя YHWH в буквальном слое оставлено как есть; в драматическом слое — «Господь», по Синодальному переводу.
Синодальный перевод передаёт тирош как «вина» без уточнения «молодое»; в литературном слое выбрано «молодое вино», как требует слово (сусло).

Слово «תלי» (teli): в буквальном слое «колчан», как в Синодальном; Раши видит здесь «меч», это оставлено в примечании. «Дичь» в Синодальном переводе точно передаёт «цайид», так что здесь критика KJV не требует русского аналога.

Игра слов Иаков (Яаков) / «запнул» (вайяʿкевени): Синодальный перевод передаёт глагол как «запнул», сохраняя образ пятки, но теряя звуковую связь с именем; в буквальном слое сохранён глагол от пятки («пяточил»), в драматическом — «подставил пятку», в комментарии связь с именем объяснена. Созвучие бехора / браха («первородство» / «благословение») по-русски не передаётся и объяснено в комментарии.

agent_notes: Предлог «מִן» в «מִשְׁמַנֵּי… וּמִטַּל» сохранён как «от» в буквальном слое (так же в Синодальном), чтобы двусмысленность осталась открытой; в драматическом слое выбрано привативное чтение «вдали от», как и в английском слое.
«מטעמים» передано как «кушанья, приготовленные по вкусу» (Синодальный: «кушанье»). Однокоренное слово «вкус» в русском сохраняет связь с «таам».
תָּרִיד передан в буквальном слое как «будешь беспокоен» (корень רוד), без выбора в пользу «господствовать»; Синодальное «воспротивишься» ближе к первому чтению, это отмечено в комментарии.
מִתְנַחֵם передан «утешается», в драматическом слое «утешает себя»: сохранена двусмысленность, которую обсуждают комментаторы; Синодальное «грозит убить» её упрощает.
В Синодальном тексте есть вставка [в Месопотамию], которой нет в иврите; в буквальном слое её нет, и комментарий это отмечает одной фразой.

history.note: [consider] Say here, too, that the Synodal keeps the sense 'obey' but drops 'голос', so that vv. 8, 13 and 43 agree. (GEN.27.8: "שְׁמַע בְּקֹלִי"; RusSynodal: "послушайся слов моих")

notes.note: Everything in 27:1-46 is covered by an event. Isaac's blessing of Jacob (27:28-29) and of Esau (27:39-40) are human blessings with a prophetic character, not divine speech, so I wrote no FULFILLS_PROPHECY link inside the chapter. Their fulfilments (Edom's revolt under Joram, 2 Kgs 8:20-22; Jacob's descendants ruling) lie in other books; a session on those chapters can write the links. Rebekah's promise 'I will send and fetch you' (27:45) is never shown fulfilled. Rebekah's earlier oracle (25:23, 'the elder shall serve the younger') would be the cause of the blessing event, but I did not link it because I cannot see that event's id in the packet. The ontologist or a later pass can add it.

[event:evt.gen_27.isaac_commissions_esau] The text gives no number for Isaac's age, only 'old' and 'dim eyes'. I anchor on his birth with 123 years, which is Rashi's count at 27:2 (from Seder Olam: Isaac 123, Jacob 63). That gives c. 1943 BCE, which is later than Esau's marriage at 40 (c. 1967 BCE, Gen 26:34) and agrees with Jacob 63. The margin of 5 years covers the uncertainty of the count. The tier is MACRO_ERA because the age comes from the tradition and not from the text. Against the anchor chain, anchor.jacob_birth plus 63 years would give about the same date.

[event:evt.gen_27.isaac_commissions_esau] Targum Pseudo-Jonathan sets the scene on the night of 14 Nisan (Passover night) at 27:1 and 27:6. This is a midrashic dating that the Hebrew does not support, so I did not use it. The day, the season and the hour stay open.

[event:evt.gen_27.esau_hunts] Duration of 3 hours is an estimate, enough for a hunt and a meal to be prepared. The text gives no figure. Rebekah and Jacob must finish before Esau returns (27:30); Esau's return is anchored on the end of the blessing.

[event:evt.gen_27.rebekah_plan] I merged 27:6-13: Rebekah's proposal, Jacob's objection (27:11-12) and her answer (27:13) are one continuous conversation with no gap. 27:5 (Rebekah overhears) is covered by the hunting event and the start of this one.

[event:evt.gen_27.kids_prepared] 27:14-17 merged: fetching the kids, cooking, dressing Jacob in Esau's garments and the goatskins. Duration of 2 hours is an estimate. The flock is near; no travel time was computed.

[event:evt.gen_27.esau_grudge] 27:41 gives no delay. I start it an hour after the lesser blessing, with a margin of a day, since the verse reports Esau's reaction and inner words. The tier is DAY_SEQUENCE because the scene is a continuation of the day.

[event:evt.gen_27.rebekah_warns_jacob] 'It was told to Rebekah' (27:42) gives no interval. I take one day, give or take three days. 'A few days' (27:44) is the length Rebekah expects the stay in Haran to last, and the later chapters show twenty years (31:38). Ibn Ezra reads 'yamim achadim' as a few years (fewer than ten), Radak as 'few'. The stay is not an event of this chapter; Gen 28-29 will record the journey. Travel from Beersheba to Haran by `urim travel` belongs to that chapter.

[event:evt.gen_27.rebekah_complains_to_isaac] 27:46 is Rebekah's pretext for sending Jacob away, with Isaac's reply and sending in 28:1-5. I put it one day after the warning with a margin of five days. It could be before the warning to Jacob (the order of verses is not a chronological claim), but I follow the verse order.
[entity:person.israel] Jacob is the corpus entity person.israel (registry id Israel@Gen.25.26-Rev, the patriarch). Not a new entity.

[entity:person.rebekah] Dropped comp.rebekah.attitude_to_hittite_wives.1 on review: comp.rebekah.grief.1 (BITTERNESS_OF_SPIRIT, Gen 26:35) is still in force at 27:46, where Rebekah says 'I am weary of my life because of the daughters of Heth' (qatsti bechayyai).

[entity:person.heth] Defined from the registry (Heth@Gen.10.15-Ezk). He is only the eponymous ancestor of the 'daughters of Heth' (27:46); the Hittite women themselves are the existing group.hittites. Heth is MENTIONED in the last event.
[entity:person.israel] Jacob is the corpus entity person.israel (registry id Israel@Gen.25.26-Rev, the patriarch). Not a new entity.

[event_links:evt.gen_27.isaac_commissions_esau] Place: no scene is named in the chapter. Every event is placed at loc.beersheba, where Isaac's dwelling was last fixed (comp.isaac.dwelling.4, Gen 26:23) and from which Jacob leaves in Gen 28:10. Inferred, not read.
[event_links:evt.gen_27.esau_hunts] Rebekah is PRESENT as the eavesdropper (27:5); she does not act in this event. Esau's hunting ground ('the field') has no identifiable location.

[entity:artifact.esaus_garments] Artifact defined because the disguise turns on it ('the best garments of Esau', 27:15, smelled at 27:27). Not given a holder before 27:15 (Rebekah's house keeping) to avoid inventing a state.

[entity:substance.savory_food] Defined as a substance because the deception and the blessing both hinge on the matammim (27:4, 7, 9, 14, 17, 31). The two kids are not modelled separately; artifact.kid_of_goats of Gen 38 is a different animal.
[component:comp.israel.disguise.1] Closed at 27:30 in esau_returns: the text says Jacob had scarcely left; the disguise end is inferred.
[component:comp.esau.allegiance.1] Read from Isaac's words 'you shall serve your brother' (27:40); a prophecy of future relationship, recorded from the blessing's verse, not an immediate service.
[component:comp.israel.lordship.1] Grounded in 27:29 and Isaac's retelling at 27:37 ('I have made him lord over you'). Value expressed through target Esau.

[system:sys.patriarchal_blessing] Defined as new rather than reused: sys.priestly_blessing (Gen 14) is cultic, sys.divine_blessing_fertility is God acting directly. Here the father speaks a binding, irrevocable blessing (27:33, 35, 37).
[system:sys.deceptive_impersonation] Defined as new; sys.wife_passed_as_sister (Gen 12) is a different, narrower deception. Categorised SOCIAL_CUSTOM since no better category fits.

[instance:inst.gen_27.lesser_blessing_of_esau] 27:39–40 is a blessing in form but reads as a contrasting oracle ('away from the fat of the earth'); reviewers may prefer to see it as PROPHETIC_ORACLE. Kept as an instance of the patriarchal blessing.
[event_links:evt.gen_27.rebekah_warns_jacob] Haran is MENTIONED only (flight destination, 27:43); Laban likewise. Rebekah's source of knowledge of Esau's words (27:42) is left open in the text.
